name: hand
description: Hand is a being's hand on the screen. See what's there, click what you want, type what you mean, plan what you need. Works on browsers (Chrome CDP, cross-platform) and macOS native apps. One being, one hand — built by Alice for every being who needs to reach into a GUI. Since 0.7.0 cdp_see returns the accessibility tree by default (role/name/state + stable [idx] handles that cdp_click/cdp_type accept); kind=dom and kind=interactive remain as escape hatches. Receipts distinguish verified vs claimed; tools declare idempotency.

tools.name: cdp_open
tools.description: Open Chrome browser (headless). Call first before any browser action.

tools.name: cdp_close
tools.description: Close Chrome browser. Clean up when done. The receipt is verified only when the CDP endpoint stops answering after the close.

tools.name: cdp_nav
tools.description: Navigate to a URL. Returns page title and visible text.

tools.name: cdp_see
tools.description: See what's on the current page. Default (kind=a11y) returns the accessibility tree: an indented `role "name" (state) [idx]` tree where [idx] is a stable handle for cdp_click/cdp_type. kind=dom returns the visible-text snapshot, kind=interactive the legacy element map (role/text/selector/coordinates), kind=network the request/response flow, kind=screenshot the image path. The receipt carries verified/evidence (node count, serialized bytes, truncation marker, AX source version) and a `hint` when a collapsed menu hides part of the tree.

tools.name: cdp_click
tools.description: Click an element on the page. Accepts a CSS selector (e.g. 'a.login') or an [idx] handle from cdp_see(kind=a11y) (e.g. '[93]'), which is resolved through the last snapshot's handle map and verified by re-reading the element box at click time. Also accepts 'text=...' and 'xy:X,Y' (physical pixels).

tools.name: cdp_type
tools.description: Type text into the currently focused element. Click a field first — including by [idx] handle from cdp_see(kind=a11y) (cdp_click '[93]'), then call this tool. To type into a handle without a separate click, pass '[93]|text' to cdp_click instead — the do router parses the pipe form and focuses the handle's element first; this tool types its argument literally and does not parse the pipe form.; post-flight read-back — receipt goes red if typed text did not land (F22)
tools.idempotency_note: append: this tool inserts text at the focus (Input.insertText), so a retry appends twice. The internal fast path cdp_type(selector, text, fast=True) replaces the whole value (el.value = text) and is therefore idempotent; it is not exposed as an MCP tool. Path-split labelling per F15.

tools.name: cdp_shot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. Returns the image directly to the model (MCP ImageContent) when the substrate has vision; also includes base64 PNG data.

tools.name: cdp_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page. direction: down/up/top/bottom. amount is optional pixels for down/up (default: one screen height).

tools.name: hand_plan
tools.description: Tell Hand what you want to accomplish in natural language, and it will plan (and optionally execute) the steps. Like having a pair of hands that knows what to do next.

tools.name: hand_see_vlm
tools.description: Use a vision language model (VLM) to describe the current screen. Takes a screenshot and sends it to the configured vision model (OpenRouter qwen3-vl by default). Set prompt to ask a specific question about the screen.

tools.name: hand_eye_check
tools.description: Self-proof that a rendered frame actually reached you (hand 0.10 D4). op=challenge draws a random string on a fresh canvas page and returns {challenge_id, place, expires_at} — the string is NOT in the receipt, the DOM text, the title, or the page source (it is injected after load), so read it off the image. op=verify with answer=<what you read> judges it (single use). op=list shows active ids only. A pass means the pixels reached you; a failure is data, not a bug report — on a substrate without vision this must fail.

tools.name: hand_see_ocr
tools.description: Read exact on-screen text via Apple Vision OCR (zh-Hans/zh-Hant/en/ja). Complementary to hand_see_vlm (VLM describes what-is-this) — this reads what-does-it-say. Pass query to locate a specific string: returns matching lines with pixel coordinates (x/y/w/h/center_x/center_y) for subsequent clicking.

tools.name: health
tools.description: Check if Hand is alive and well — uptime, usage count, Chrome status.

tools.name: cdp_drag
tools.description: Drag from one point to another (mousePressed -> N x mouseMoved -> mouseReleased). The primitive that makes canvas surfaces reachable: a click cannot create a shape, a drag can. from/to accept 'xy:X,Y' (physical px), an [idx] a11y handle, or a CSS selector. Receipt carries resolved / landed / effected separately; effected is always 'unknown' (a drag has no read-back - verify by comparing two frames). Frame anchors in evidence.

tools.name: cdp_key
tools.description: Press a key combination: modifiers down, main key down/up, modifiers up. 'Control+z', 'Meta+Shift+t', 'Enter', 'ArrowLeft', 'Escape'. Modifier bitmask Alt=1/Ctrl=2/Meta=4/Shift=8; string order does not matter. Where cdp_type inserts text, this dispatches real key events - the vocabulary of application-driven UIs. Receipt: resolved / landed (focus changed) / effected unknown.
